content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Is there a budget-friendly way to convert a CAN Bus value (from a third-party battery management system, such as state of charge) into a [product_name] Modbus TCP or [version_no] value? I plan to convert the float to an integer for use in my application. Best regards, [user_name]

Greetings [user_name], [product_name] units starting from [version_no] support Modbus TCP, but to connect with a CAN device, you will need a gateway. We've frequently worked with gateways from Anybus in our projects; they are cost-effective, reliable, and their configuration software is user-friendly. Check their product page for more details—there is a Case Studies section with examples on Modbus TCP/CAN communicators: [url] Hope this provides some guidance, [user_name]
Thanks [user_name], I've reached out to the provider for pricing updates. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for practical ways to connect CAN Bus data from external battery management systems to [product_name] devices via Modbus TCP or [version_no] protocols. While Modbus TCP is supported, a clear and affordable solution for bridging CAN Bus data is less obvious, suggesting the need for more accessible interoperability options or guidance within the [company_name] ecosystem.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy-to-implement and affordable approach to convert CAN Bus signals from third-party equipment into values that are compatible with [company_name] systems via Modbus TCP or [version_no], enabling seamless data integration with [product_name] applications.
